handbookNote: Michigan Notary Public Act, 2003 PA 238, MCL 55.261-55.315 (37 sections, fetched verbatim from legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-16). Classification: APPLICATION-ONLY -- confirmed via MCL 55.271 qualifications (18+, MI residency OR a principal place of business in MI, English literacy, no disqualifying felony/misdemeanor/violation) which impose no exam or training mandate on the notary applicant personally. This is NOT exam prep; it is a self-study/reference practice-question set covering real state notary law, priced and framed accordingly. IMPORTANT MYTH-BUSTING NOTE: MCL 55.277 creates a 'notary education and training fund,' but per 55.277(4) that fund pays GRANTS to county clerks and their staff for training on notary responsibilities/election work -- it is emphatically NOT a requirement that individual notary applicants complete any training or coursework. Copy for this track must never imply notaries themselves must complete training. UNUSUAL/CONFIRMED DUAL-AUTHORITY STRUCTURE: although the Secretary of State is the sole appointing authority (MCL 55.269(1)), MCL 55.271(1)(f) and 55.273(1) require the applicant to, within the 90 days before filing the SOS application, appear IN PERSON before the COUNTY CLERK of their residence (or expected appointment) to file a $10,000 surety bond and take an oath, plus pay a $10 county filing fee (55.273(2)-(3)) -- and MCL 55.271(2) requires the SOS to notify each county clerk's office monthly of new appointments in that county. This genuine dual state/county administrative structure (not a myth) is reflected throughout the commissioning-bucket questions. CONTENT DEPTH RATIONALE: despite application-only classification, the statute has real substantive depth that supports a full practice-question bank -- particularly the remote/electronic notarization provisions (55.286, 286a-d: electronic notarization system approval, RON platform approval and journal/recording retention rules, and the now-superseded pandemic-era 2-way audiovisual bridge under 286c/286d) and the misconduct/discipline/penalty provisions (55.295-55.309: SOS investigation and complaint process, civil liability, administrative penalties up to a $1,000 fine, automatic revocation for felony/imprisonment, and criminal penalties escalating to a 4-year felony for real-estate-related violations). 127 grounded questions across 7 topic buckets, each citing a specific MCL 55.2xx subsection; no invented facts, no padding to hit an artificial target. PRICING: $0.75 (75 cents) per 2026-08-16 site-owner pricing directive for this state -- Michigan has no confirmed graded assessment of any kind (application-only, like AL/county-run states get this project's lowest tier), so this is education-only practice content rather than exam prep, priced well below the $9.99 exam-state Notary tier.
